+import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bits
+import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog
+import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.SymbolLift
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 0
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+/-!
+# Machine-construction library: configuration records over a rich alphabet (§12.8)
+
+The record carrier of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design
+(`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a §2, decision 12.8.1): a configuration of a
+`Bool` machine with work tapes inside a radius-`s` window, written as a list of
+fields over the rich alphabet `Turing.RecSym`. Records are what the
+configuration-graph searches of chapter 4 (the reachability simulation of
+`NSPACE` in `DSPACE` by breadth-first search, Savitch's midpoint recursion)
+keep on their tapes, and the record rows are the machines that read, step and
+compare them.
+
+**Status: statements.** The carrier, the record and its predicates are real
+definitions, and `Turing.cfgRecord_length` is proved. Every other result is
+sorried with a proof sketch, pending the §12.8 fill: the pure decoding facts
+and the three record rows.
+
+## Design
+
+* **One cell per simulated cell.** A tape field holds the `2s + 1` window cells
+  of one work tape, each a content track and a head-mark track
+  (`Turing.RecSym.cell`). The input position is a fixed-width binary field of
+  digits, `O(log n)` cells, and the state and the tag take one cell each. A
+  record therefore has `k(2s + 1) + posWidth n + 2` cells and `k + 2`
+  separators, which is `O(S n)` at radius `O(S n)` for `S ≥ log`.
+* **Blank-separated fields** (`Turing.joinFields`): every field is a §12.6
+  delimited word in place (`Turing.fieldsTape_field`), so the framed catalog
+  rows apply field by field, and no field is empty, so two blanks end a table.
+* **Digits are the lift's `e`.** `Turing.RecSym.digitEmb` is the embedding
+  along which the `Bool` counter rows run on rich tapes
+  (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`), and the native input of a rich
+  simulator is the input's image under it.
+* **The window predicate** `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` lives here, relocated
+  verbatim from `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBF` (decision 12.8.2), which
+  now imports it, so the record carrier and the adjacency codec share one
+  definition.
+* **Record rows are existential modules** in the `exists_installCallTM` style:
+  a machine, entry and verdict anchors, and a linear first-return bound, with
+  every head, the input position and the scratch restored.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` — the radius-`s` window predicate (relocated).
+* `Turing.RecSym`, `Turing.RecSym.digitEmb` — the record alphabet and its
+  digit embedding.
+* `Turing.binDigits`, `Turing.posWidth` — fixed-width binary digits and the
+  input-position width.
+* `Turing.cfgRecord` — the record of a configuration.
+* `Turing.RecordValid`, `Turing.RecordAt` — valid records, and a record laid
+  out at a head.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.cfgRecord_length` — a record has `k + 3` fields.
+* `Turing.cfgRecord_inj` — on windowed configurations, records agree exactly
+  when configuration cores and tags do (statement).
+* `Turing.recordValid_iff` — validity as a field-by-field shape condition
+  (statement).
+* `Turing.exists_recordStepTM`, `Turing.exists_recordEqTM`,
+  `Turing.exists_recordTestTM` — the record rows R8.7: one simulated step, record
+  equality, and a test of the state and tag (statements).
+
+## References
+
+* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
+  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1: the configuration graph and
+  Claim 4.4(1), the `O(S(n))`-bit description of a configuration;
+  Theorem 4.2(iii) and Theorem 4.14 (Savitch), whose simulations search the
+  graph keeping configuration descriptions on work tapes. The record adds an
+  `O(log n)` input-position field, as the book's description does.)
+-/
+
+namespace Turing
+
+/-! ### The window predicate -/
+
+/-- A configuration lies **in the radius-`s` window** when every work head
+sits within `[-s, s]` and every work cell outside `[-s, s]` is blank — the
+side condition under which the packaged codec of
+`Complexity.exists_adjacency_codec_cnf` is faithful. (The input head needs no
+clause: its type bounds it.) It is equally the side condition under which a
+configuration record determines its configuration core, together with its
+separately supplied tag (`Turing.cfgRecord_inj`);
+relocated here from `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBF` (decision 12.8.2). -/
+def Cfg.InWindow {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type} {x : List Symbol} (s : ℕ)
+    (c : Cfg k Symbol State x) : Prop :=
+  (∀ i, |c.workTapePos i| ≤ (s : ℤ)) ∧
+  ∀ (i : Fin k) (z : ℤ), (s : ℤ) < |z| → c.workTapes i z = none
+
+/-! ### The record alphabet -/
+
+/-- **The record alphabet** (design §12.8a §2) over machine states `Q` and tags
+`T`: binary digits, simulated work cells with a head-mark track, the state
+cell, and the tag cell. Fields of a record are separated by blank cells. -/
+inductive RecSym (Q T : Type) where
+  /-- a binary digit: the input-position field, counters, and the native input -/
+  | digit (b : Bool)
+  /-- one simulated work cell: its content and whether the head is on it -/
+  | cell (content : Option Bool) (mark : Bool)
+  /-- the state cell, `none` for halted -/
+  | st (q : Option Q)
+  /-- the tag cell: a summary of what the run has emitted -/
+  | tag (τ : T)
+deriving DecidableEq
+
+/-- The record alphabet is finite when the states and tags are; this is the
+`Fintype` instance `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` needs. -/
+instance recSymFintype (Q T : Type) [Fintype Q] [Fintype T] : Fintype (RecSym Q T) :=
+  derive_fintype% _
+
+/-- **The digit embedding** (design §12.8a §2): `Bool` into the record alphabet
+by `Turing.RecSym.digit`. It is the `e` along which `Bool` rows and the `Bool`
+input are lifted to rich tapes (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`). -/
+def RecSym.digitEmb (Q T : Type) : Bool ↪ RecSym Q T :=
+  ⟨RecSym.digit, fun _ _ h => by cases h; rfl⟩
+
+/-! ### The record -/
+
+/-- **Fixed-width binary digits** (design §12.8a §2): the `w` low bits of `v`,
+least significant first. -/
+def binDigits (w v : ℕ) : List Bool := (List.range w).map v.testBit
+
+/-- **The input-position width** (design §12.8a §2) at input length `n`: the
+bit length of `n + 1`, so that `2 ^ posWidth n > n + 1` and every input
+position `0, …, n + 1` has a distinct `Turing.binDigits` code. -/
+def posWidth (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length
+
+/-- **The configuration record** (design §12.8a §2) of `c` at window radius
+`s` with tag `τ`: `k + 3` fields. Field `0` is the state, field `1` the input
+position in `Turing.binDigits` of width `Turing.posWidth |x|`, fields `2` to
+`k + 1` the window cells `-s, …, s` of each work tape with their head marks,
+and field `k + 2` the tag. The output tape is not recorded; the tag summarizes
+it. -/
+def cfgRecord {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) :
+    List (List (RecSym Q T)) :=
+  [RecSym.st c.state] ::
+    ((binDigits (posWidth x.length) c.inputPos.val).map RecSym.digit) ::
+    (((List.finRange k).map fun i => (List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
+      RecSym.cell (c.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s)) (decide (c.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s))) ++
+    [[RecSym.tag τ]])
+
+/-- **Record length** (design §12.8a §2): a record has `k + 3` fields, whatever
+the configuration, radius and tag. -/
+theorem cfgRecord_length {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x)
+    (τ : T) : (cfgRecord s c τ).length = k + 3 := by
+  simp [cfgRecord]
+
+/-- **Canonical decoding** (design §12.8a §2). On windowed configurations of
+one input, records agree exactly when the configurations agree on state, input
+position, work tapes and work heads, and the tags agree. The output is not
+compared, so this is injectivity on the configuration core, the vertex
+quotient of the configuration graph.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Compare the fields. The state field gives the state. The
+position field is `Turing.binDigits` at a width with `2 ^ posWidth |x| >
+|x| + 1`, which is injective on values `≤ |x| + 1`, the range of input
+positions. For tape `i`, the content track gives the cells in `[-s, s]`, and
+outside it both configurations are blank by the window hypothesis. The mark
+track has exactly one mark, at the head, which lies in `[-s, s]`. The tag field
+gives the tag. -/
+theorem cfgRecord_inj {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) {c d : Cfg k Bool Q x}
+    {τ τ' : T} (hc : c.InWindow s) (hd : d.InWindow s) :
+    cfgRecord s c τ = cfgRecord s d τ' ↔
+      (c.state = d.state ∧ c.inputPos = d.inputPos ∧ c.workTapes = d.workTapes ∧
+        c.workTapePos = d.workTapePos) ∧ τ = τ' := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- **Valid records** (design §12.8a §2): the field list is the record, at
+radius `s`, of some windowed configuration on some input of length `n`, with
+some tag. -/
+def RecordValid (k n s : ℕ) (Q T : Type) (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) : Prop :=
+  ∃ (x : List Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), x.length = n ∧ c.InWindow s ∧
+    cfgRecord s c τ = fs
+
+/-- **Validity is a shape condition** (design §12.8a §2). A field list is a
+valid record exactly when it has `k + 3` fields: a state cell; `posWidth n`
+digits of a value at most `n + 1`; for each tape, `2s + 1` work cells of which
+exactly one carries the head mark; and a tag cell. This shape supports a
+validity machine built from finite-state folds over the fields, given the
+widths `2s + 1` and `posWidth n` and the bound `n + 1` as templates or
+counters. A fold of one field alone cannot check a variable width: a single
+marked cell is valid at `s = 0` and not at `s = 1`. The validator itself is
+deferred to S1b's statement phase.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Forward: read the shape off `Turing.cfgRecord`, with the mark
+at index `pos + s` of each tape field, which is in range by the window
+hypothesis. Backward: take the input `List.replicate n false`, the state and
+the tag from their cells, the input position from the digits, and for tape `i`
+the cell at `z` from index `z + s` of its field when `|z| ≤ s`, and blank
+otherwise, with the head at the mark minus `s`. This configuration is windowed
+and its record is the given list. -/
+theorem recordValid_iff {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (n s : ℕ) (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) :
+    RecordValid k n s Q T fs ↔
+      fs.length = k + 3 ∧
+      (∃ q : Option Q, fs[0]? = some [RecSym.st q]) ∧
+      (∃ v ≤ n + 1, fs[1]? = some ((binDigits (posWidth n) v).map RecSym.digit)) ∧
+      (∀ i : Fin k, ∃ (cs : ℕ → Option Bool) (m : ℕ), m < 2 * s + 1 ∧
+        fs[i.val + 2]? = some ((List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
+          RecSym.cell (cs j) (decide (j = m)))) ∧
+      (∃ τ : T, fs[k + 2]? = some [RecSym.tag τ]) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- **A record at a head** (design §12.8a §2): tape `r` holds the field layout
+of `fs` from its head, delimited by blanks at relative positions `-1` and
+`|joinFields fs|`. The cells beyond the delimiters are arbitrary. -/
+def RecordAt {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} (d : Cfg K Γ S x) (r : Fin K)
+    (fs : List (List Γ)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields fs).length : ℤ) →
+    d.workTapes r (d.workTapePos r + p) = fieldsTape fs p
+
+/-! ### R8.7 — the record rows -/
+
+/-- **R8.7, one simulated step** (design §12.8a §3, GAP-4). For a fixed `Bool`
+machine `M` and a tag update `upd` that ignores silent steps, there is a module
+over the record alphabet with an entry and two distinct verdict anchors with
+the following contract. Start it at its entry with the record of a windowed
+configuration `c` at the head of tape `0`, its other tapes blank, and the
+native input `x` as digits. It reaches a verdict within `C` times the record
+length plus `|x| + 1`, and no verdict earlier. If `M.step c` is windowed, the
+verdict is `yes` and the record interval holds the record of `M.step c`, with
+tag `upd τ (M.outputSymbol c)`; otherwise the verdict is `no` and nothing has
+changed. In both cases every head, the input position, the other tapes and the
+output are restored. Up to the verdict every work head stays within `C` times
+the record length plus one of its entry position. So the module's work space
+is linear in the record length, however far the native input head travels.
+It depends on `|x|` only through the `posWidth |x|` position digits. A halted
+`c` steps to itself with its tag
+unchanged, by `hupd`.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Compose by R2 seams, with no private trace. Read: `scanTM`
+folds collect the state, the tag, and for each tape field the marked cell's
+content and whether the mark is at an edge, moving between fields by `skipTM`.
+Read the input symbol. The host's input position is arbitrary, so first save
+it in binary on a scratch digit tape: a counter of width `posWidth |x|`, which
+holds every input position since positions are at most `|x| + 1`. Then copy
+the position field to another scratch digit tape (`copyTM`), run the lifted
+`exists_inputSeekTM` on it, read the symbol, and restore the saved position.
+At `|x| = 0`, which the one-digit position width reveals, the input is blank
+and the head need not move. Dispatch on `M.tr` over the finite data. Apply: `scanTM` maps rewrite
+the marked content, the state and the tag; delay steps shift the marks; the
+position field moves by the lifted increment or decrement on the scratch tape,
+clamped at `0` and `|x| + 1` as `moveInputPos` clamps, and is copied back. A
+mark leaving the window selects `no` before anything is written. Rewind by
+`skipBackTM`. Each phase takes time linear in the record length or in `|x|`.
+Its work heads move only over the record and over scratch words of the
+position width, hence within `O(L + 1)` cells. -/
+theorem exists_recordStepTM {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} [Fintype Q] [DecidableEq Q] [Fintype T]
+    [DecidableEq T] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool Q) (upd : T → Option Bool → T)
+    (hupd : ∀ τ, upd τ none = τ) :
+    ∃ (K : ℕ) (P : Type) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : DecidableEq P)
+      (R : MultiTapeTM (K + 1) (RecSym Q T) P) (entry yes no : P) (C : ℕ), yes ≠ no ∧
+      ∀ {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), c.InWindow s →
+      ∀ d : Cfg (K + 1) (RecSym Q T) P (x.map (RecSym.digitEmb Q T)),
+        d.state = some entry → RecordAt d 0 (cfgRecord s c τ) →
+        (∀ j : Fin (K + 1), j ≠ 0 → ∀ p, d.workTapes j p = none) →
+        ∃ t ≤ C * ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length + x.length + 1),
+          (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some yes ∧ (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some no) ∧
+          (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin (K + 1),
+            |(R.runFrom d u).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
+              ((C * ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
+          ((M.step c).InWindow s →
+            R.runFrom d t =
+              { d with
+                state := some yes
+                workTapes := fun j q =>
+                  if j = 0 ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧
+                      q < d.workTapePos j + ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length : ℤ)
+                    then fieldsTape (cfgRecord s (M.step c) (upd τ (M.outputSymbol c)))
+                      (q - d.workTapePos j)
+                  else d.workTapes j q }) ∧
+          (¬ (M.step c).InWindow s → R.runFrom d t = { d with state := some no }) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- **R8.7, record equality** (design §12.8a §3). There is a two-tape module
+over the record alphabet with an entry and two distinct verdict anchors with
+the following contract. Start it at its entry with field lists `fs` and `gs`,
+of `k + 3` fields each, laid out at the heads of tapes `0` and `1`. It reaches
+`yes` if `fs = gs` and `no` otherwise, within `C` times the length of `fs`'s
+layout plus one, with no verdict earlier and nothing else changed. Up to the
+verdict both heads stay within that many cells of their entry positions,
+however long `gs` is. The input is arbitrary and not read.
+
+**Proof sketch.** For each of the `k + 3` fields, run `compareTM` framed
+(`compareTM_run_ofCfg`) on the two current fields; on `false`, return `no`, and
+on `true`, `skipTM` both tapes to the next field. After the last field, return
+`yes`. Before the verdict, `skipBackTM` both heads over the fields crossed,
+which have the same lengths on both tapes. Every phase is linear in the cells
+of `fs` crossed. -/
+theorem exists_recordEqTM (k : ℕ) (Q T : Type) [Fintype Q] [DecidableEq Q] [Fintype T]
+    [DecidableEq T] :
+    ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : DecidableEq P) (R : MultiTapeTM 2 (RecSym Q T) P)
+      (entry yes no : P) (C : ℕ), yes ≠ no ∧
+      ∀ {x : List (RecSym Q T)} (fs gs : List (List (RecSym Q T))),
+        fs.length = k + 3 → gs.length = k + 3 →
+      ∀ d : Cfg 2 (RecSym Q T) P x, d.state = some entry → RecordAt d 0 fs → RecordAt d 1 gs →
+        ∃ t ≤ C * ((joinFields fs).length + 1),
+          (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some yes ∧ (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some no) ∧
+          (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin 2,
+            |(R.runFrom d u).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
+              ((C * ((joinFields fs).length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
+          R.runFrom d t = { d with state := some (if fs = gs then yes else no) } := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- **R8.7, a test of state and tag** (design §12.8a §3). For a predicate `P`
+on states and tags, there is a one-tape module over the record alphabet with an
+entry and two distinct verdict anchors with the following contract. Start it
+at its entry with the record of `c` with tag `τ` at its head. It reaches `yes`
+if `P c.state τ` and `no` otherwise, within `C` times the record length plus
+one, with no verdict earlier and nothing else changed. Up to the verdict its
+head stays within that many cells of its entry position. Consumers host it on a
+record tape by R1 (`embedEmitTM`); the table search of the reachability
+simulation tests for a halted accepting record this way.
+
+**Proof sketch.** A `scanTM` fold reads the state field; `skipTM` crosses the
+`k + 2` fields to the tag, a second fold reads the tag, and `skipBackTM`
+returns over the fields crossed. Dispatch on `P` over the finite data. -/
+theorem exists_recordTestTM {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} [Fintype Q] [DecidableEq Q] [Fintype T]
+    [DecidableEq T] (P : Option Q → T → Bool) :
+    ∃ (P' : Type) (_ : Fintype P') (_ : DecidableEq P') (R : MultiTapeTM 1 (RecSym Q T) P')
+      (entry yes no : P') (C : ℕ), yes ≠ no ∧
+      ∀ {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) {y : List (RecSym Q T)}
+        (d : Cfg 1 (RecSym Q T) P' y), d.state = some entry →
+        RecordAt d 0 (cfgRecord s c τ) →
+        ∃ t ≤ C * ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length + 1),
+          (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some yes ∧ (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some no) ∧
+          (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin 1,
+            |(R.runFrom d u).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
+              ((C * ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
+          R.runFrom d t = { d with state := some (if P c.state τ then yes else no) } := by
+  sorry
+
+end Turing

@@ -1200,4 +1207,69 @@ theorem counterLoop_time_le {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
       Nat.add_le_add (by simpa using hsum) hc
     _ = _ := by omega
 
+/-! ## R8.6 — the expansion (§12.8) -/
+
+/-- **R8.6, the expansion** (design §12.8a). The counter loop whose round is
+the advancing writer: with a counter of value `d` on the last tape, it writes
+the pattern `pat` on tape `i` `d` times, contiguously from the head, and leaves
+the head after the last copy. Its uses are lengths given in binary: the
+window halves of a record, of length `d·|pat|` for a radius counter `d`. -/
+def expandTM (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (pat : List Bool) :
+    MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Bool (CounterLoopState (Fin (pat.length + 1))) :=
+  counterLoopTM (writeAdvTM k i pat) 0 none
+
+/-- **R8.6, the expansion, framed** (design §12.8a). Start the expansion at its
+decrement phase with body configuration `c` at the writer's state `0` and the
+delimited counter word `w`, of value `d`, at `cp`. It reaches `done` at exactly
+`d·(|pat| + 1) + counterOverhead w (d + 1)` and neither exit anchor earlier.
+At that point the interval `[pos, pos + d·|pat|)` of tape `i` holds `d` copies
+of `pat`, whatever it held before, the head of tape `i` is at `pos + d·|pat|`,
+the counter is all `true` with its head back at `cp`, and every other cell,
+every other head, the input position and the output are unchanged. Throughout,
+the counter head stays within `[cp - 1, cp + |w|]`, the head of tape `i`
+within `[pos, pos + d·|pat|]`, and every other body head is fixed.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Apply `Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done` with the constant round
+time `τ := |pat| + 1`. The round hypotheses are `Turing.writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg`
+at the orbit's `r`-th configuration, which by induction on `r` has `r` copies
+of `pat` written from `pos` and its head at `pos + r·|pat|`. The round sum is
+`d·(|pat| + 1)`. The head clauses follow from the loop's trajectory clause and
+the writer's. -/
+theorem expandTM_run_ofCfg {k : ℕ} {x : List Bool} (i : Fin k) (pat : List Bool)
+    (c : Cfg k Bool (Fin (pat.length + 1)) x) (hc : c.state = some 0)
+    (w : List Bool) (ct : ℤ → Option Bool) (cp : ℤ)
+    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) → ct (cp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape w p)
+    (d : ℕ) (hd : Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) = d) :
+    (expandTM k i pat).runFrom (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp)
+        (d * (pat.length + 1) + counterOverhead w (d + 1)) =
+      counterLoopCfg (some .done)
+        { c with
+          workTapes := fun j q =>
+            if j = i ∧ c.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧
+                q < c.workTapePos j + ((d * pat.length : ℕ) : ℤ)
+              then FinTM.bufferTape (List.replicate d pat).flatten (q - c.workTapePos j)
+            else c.workTapes j q
+          workTapePos := Function.update c.workTapePos i
+            (c.workTapePos i + ((d * pat.length : ℕ) : ℤ)) }
+        (fun q => if cp ≤ q ∧ q < cp + (w.length : ℤ) then some true else ct q) cp ∧
+      (∀ t < d * (pat.length + 1) + counterOverhead w (d + 1),
+        ((expandTM k i pat).runFrom (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) t).state ≠
+          some .done ∧
+        ((expandTM k i pat).runFrom (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) t).state ≠
+          some .escape) ∧
+      (∀ t ≤ d * (pat.length + 1) + counterOverhead w (d + 1),
+        ((expandTM k i pat).runFrom
+            (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) t).workTapePos (Fin.last k) ∈
+          Finset.Icc (cp - 1) (cp + (w.length : ℤ))) ∧
+      (∀ t ≤ d * (pat.length + 1) + counterOverhead w (d + 1), ∀ j : Fin k,
+        if j = i then
+          ((expandTM k i pat).runFrom
+              (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) t).workTapePos j.castSucc ∈
+            Finset.Icc (c.workTapePos j) (c.workTapePos j + ((d * pat.length : ℕ) : ℤ))
+        else
+          ((expandTM k i pat).runFrom
+              (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) t).workTapePos j.castSucc =
+            c.workTapePos j) := by
+  sorry
+
 end Turing

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..14d2b96a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/InputCall.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
+-/
+import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CounterLoop
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 0
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+/-!
+# Machine-construction library: modules on the native input (§12.8)
+
+The two native-input modules of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design
+(`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a §3): a call of a function-level machine
+on the native input at a clean seam (R8.5e), and a seek of the input head to a
+position held in binary on a work tape (R8.5b). Both are `Bool` modules; a
+rich host runs them lifted along its digit embedding
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`), with unchanged time and space.
+
+**Status: statements.** Both rows are existential modules in the
+`Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM` style, sorried with construction sketches,
+pending the §12.8 fill.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.FinTM.exists_inputCallTM` — compute `f` on the native input from a
+  blank seam and install the result on tape `0` (statement).
+* `Turing.exists_inputSeekTM` — move the input head to the binary value on a
+  counter tape, restoring every work tape (statement).
+
+## References
+
+* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
+  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the read-only input tape, whose
+  head a work-tape counter can position; the space-bounded simulations of
+  §4.1 locate the input head of a simulated configuration this way.)
+-/
+
+namespace Turing.FinTM
+
+/-- **R8.5e, the clean call on the native input** (design §12.8a §3). For any
+witness `M` computing `f` within `T`, there is a callable module with entry and
+exit states and a positive tape count with the following contract. From the
+blank seam `Cfg.ofWords entry` (every tape empty, input head at `1`, empty
+output) over the native input `x`, the module reaches, at its first positive
+visit to `exit`, exactly the seam with `f x` installed on tape `0`, within
+`c·(T |x| + |x| + |f x| + 1)` steps. It is the function-level contract run at a
+seam that the next phase of a host can consume.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Seam-compose (`Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg`) the input
+copier on tape `0` (`Turing.inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg`, `2|x| + 2` steps, which
+from the blank seam yields `Cfg.ofWords` with `x` on tape `0`) with the install
+call of `Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM` on the argument `x`, whose
+coefficient absorbs the copy and the dispatch step. The first-return clause is
+`Turing.seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg`, which also needs the callee's exit
+excluded at time `0`; the install call's contract excludes it only at positive
+times. So split on whether its entry equals its exit. If it does, first wrap it
+by `Turing.seamReleaseTM`, whose `Turing.seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` supplies a
+fresh entry. The positive tape count is the install call's. -/
+theorem exists_inputCallTM (M : FinTM Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (T : ℕ → ℕ) (hM : M.ComputesFunInTime f T) :
+    ∃ (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) (c : ℕ), 0 < C.k ∧
+      ∀ x : List Bool,
+        ∃ t ≤ c * (T x.length + x.length + (f x).length + 1),
+          0 < t ∧
+          (∀ t', 0 < t' → t' < t →
+            (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) entry (fun _ => [])) t').state ≠
+              some exit) ∧
+          C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) entry (fun _ => [])) t =
+            Cfg.ofWords exit (stateWord C.k (f x)) := by
+  sorry
+
+end Turing.FinTM
+
+namespace Turing
+
+/-- **R8.5b, the input seek** (design §12.8a §3). There is a two-tape `Bool`
+module with entry and exit states with the following contract. Let tape `0`
+hold, from its head, a delimited word `w` whose little-endian value `p` is a
+valid input position, at most `|x| + 1`, and let tape `1` be blank. From the
+entry, with the input head anywhere, the module reaches `exit` with the input
+head at `p` within `C·(|w| + pos + p + 1)` steps, where `pos` is the starting
+input position, and not earlier. Every work tape, every work head and the
+output are restored. Up to the exit every work head stays within
+`C·(|w| + 1)` cells of its entry position. So the module's work space is
+`O(|w| + 1)`, however far the input head travels, and repeated calls compose.
+A rich host runs it lifted on two dedicated digit tapes.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Copy `w` to the scratch tape (`Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg`,
+`2|w| + 2`). Rewind the input head: `timed_rewind` returns it to position `1`
+within `pos + 2` steps, and one further left move reaches the left end marker
+`0`. Run `Turing.counterLoopTM` with the scratch copy as the
+counter and the one-step round "input head right", `p` rounds
+(`Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done`, `p + counterOverhead w (p + 1)`, at most
+`5p + 2|w| + 2` by `Turing.counterOverhead_le`). The counter ends all `true`
+with its head back; `Turing.clearTM_run_ofCfg` blanks it. The phases join by
+R2 seams, whose dispatch steps add a constant. The work heads move only in the
+copy, the counter loop and the clear, whose trajectory clauses keep each one
+within `[pos - 1, pos + |w|]` of its tape. -/
+theorem exists_inputSeekTM :
+    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Fintype S) (_ : DecidableEq S) (R : MultiTapeTM 2 Bool S) (entry exit : S)
+      (C : ℕ),
+      ∀ {x : List Bool} (p : ℕ) (w : List Bool), Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) = p →
+        p ≤ x.length + 1 → ∀ d : Cfg 2 Bool S x, d.state = some entry →
+        (∀ q : ℤ, -1 ≤ q → q ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
+          d.workTapes 0 (d.workTapePos 0 + q) = FinTM.bufferTape w q) →
+        (∀ q, d.workTapes 1 q = none) →
+        ∃ t ≤ C * (w.length + d.inputPos.val + p + 1),
+          (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some exit) ∧
+          (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin 2,
+            |(R.runFrom d u).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤ ((C * (w.length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
+          (R.runFrom d t).state = some exit ∧ ((R.runFrom d t).inputPos : ℕ) = p ∧
+          (R.runFrom d t).workTapes = d.workTapes ∧ (R.runFrom d t).workTapePos = d.workTapePos ∧
+          (R.runFrom d t).output = d.output := by
+  sorry
+
+end Turing
diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Scan.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Scan.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..ff12fce6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Scan.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,274 @@
+/-

+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
+-/
+import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 0
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+/-!
+# Machine-construction library: constant writers and native-input sweeps (§12.8)
+
+The single-sweep rows of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design
+(`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a) that touch no G1-owned file: two writers
+of a fixed word (R8.4, R8.4′) and two sweeps of the native input (R8.5a,
+R8.5d). They are alphabet-generic, like the G1 catalog, and they are stated in
+the §12.6 framed form: exact time, finish configuration, no earlier exit, and
+the trajectory of every head, from an arbitrary configuration.
+
+**Status: statements.** The four machines and the writers' phase alphabet are
+real definitions. Every contract is sorried with a proof sketch, pending the
+§12.8 fill.
+
+## Design
+
+* **Two writers.** `Turing.writeConstTM` writes its word and returns the head,
+  so it composes under `Turing.seamCompTM` like the R3 sweeps. The advancing
+  writer `Turing.writeAdvTM` leaves the head after the word and returns to its
+  own start state, which is the round shape of `Turing.counterLoopTM`; it is
+  the round of `Turing.expandTM` (R8.6). A seam consumer that calls it once
+  uses `Turing.seamReleaseTM`.
+* **Tables** are written with the catalog's one-tape actions
+  `Turing.tapeAction` and `Turing.inputMoveAction`.
+* **The input sweeps** move the native input head in lockstep with the work
+  heads and return it to position `1`. `Turing.inputCopyTM` reuses the sweep
+  alphabet `Turing.SweepPhase` and `Turing.inputFoldTM` the scan alphabet
+  `Turing.ScanPhase`, so no phase type is duplicated.
+* **The input fold is the validator** of design §12.8a §0: a rich
+  space-bounded simulator folds its input through `decodeBool`'s domain first
+  and stops on a foreign symbol, because `alphabet_reduction_spaceUsed` bounds
+  space over all rich inputs (decision O6).
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.WritePhase`, `Turing.writeConstTM` — write a fixed word and return.
+* `Turing.writeAdvTM` — write a fixed word and leave the head after it.
+* `Turing.inputCopyTM` — copy the native input onto a work tape.
+* `Turing.inputFoldTM` — fold the native input with a finite-state update.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.writeConstTM_run_ofCfg`, `Turing.writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg`,
+  `Turing.inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg`, `Turing.inputFoldTM_run_ofCfg` — the framed
+  contracts (statements).
+
+## References
+
+* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
+  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the k-tape model with a read-only
+  input tape; the routines are folklore subroutines of the textbook's
+  simulations. §4.1: the space measure that makes input validation necessary
+  for the rich simulators.)
+-/
+
+namespace Turing
+
+/-! ### R8.4 — the constant writer -/
+
+/-- **Phase alphabet of the constant writer** (design §12.8a, R8.4), for a word
+of length `n`: writing cell `j`, walking back with `j` cells to go, and the
+live exit anchor. -/
+inductive WritePhase (n : ℕ) where
+  /-- writing cell `j` of the word -/
+  | wr (j : Fin (n + 1))
+  /-- walking back, `j` cells from the origin -/
+  | bk (j : Fin (n + 1))
+  /-- the live exit anchor -/
+  | done
+deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
+
+/-- **R8.4, the constant writer** (design §12.8a). Write the fixed word `w₀` on
+tape `i` from its head, moving right, then walk back `|w₀|` cells and enter the
+live `done` anchor with the head where it started. The old contents of the
+tape are never read. -/
+def writeConstTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (w₀ : List Symbol) :
+    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (WritePhase w₀.length) where
+  q₀ := .wr 0
+  tr := fun q _ _ =>
+    match q with
+    | .wr j =>
+      if h : (j : ℕ) < w₀.length then
+        tapeAction i 0 (some (some w₀[(j : ℕ)])) .pos (.wr ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩)
+      else inputMoveAction 0 (.bk ⟨w₀.length, by omega⟩)
+    | .bk j =>
+      if (j : ℕ) = 0 then inputMoveAction 0 .done
+      else tapeAction i 0 none .neg (.bk ⟨j - 1, by omega⟩)
+    | .done => inputMoveAction 0 .done
+
+/-- **R8.4, the constant writer, framed** (design §12.8a). From any
+configuration at the writer's start phase, the writer reaches `done` at
+exactly `2|w₀| + 2` and not earlier. At that point the interval
+`[pos, pos + |w₀|)` of tape `i` holds `w₀`, whatever it held before, and every
+other cell, the head positions, the input position and the output are
+unchanged. Up to the exit the head of tape `i` stays within
+`[pos, pos + |w₀|]`, and every other head is fixed.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the cells written: `|w₀|` steps write `w₀` moving
+right. One stationary step turns into the walk back, `|w₀|` steps return the
+head to `pos`, and one stationary step enters `done`. No step reads a work
+cell, so the old contents are irrelevant. -/
+theorem writeConstTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
+    (w₀ : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w₀.length) x)
+    (hstate : d.state = some (.wr 0)) :
+    (writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d (2 * w₀.length + 2) =
+        { d with
+          state := some .done
+          workTapes := fun j q =>
+            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ)
+              then FinTM.bufferTape w₀ (q - d.workTapePos j)
+            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
+      (∀ t < 2 * w₀.length + 2, ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some .done) ∧
+      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * w₀.length + 2 →
+        if j = i then
+          ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
+            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j) (d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ))
+        else ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ### R8.4′ — the advancing writer -/
+
+/-- **R8.4′, the advancing writer** (design §12.8a). Write the fixed word `w₀`
+on tape `i` from its head, moving right, and return to the start state `0` with
+the head just after the word. The state `j` is the number of cells written. The
+writer is cyclic: started again, it writes `w₀` again after the first copy,
+which makes it a round body of `Turing.counterLoopTM` with anchor `0`. -/
+def writeAdvTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (w₀ : List Symbol) :
+    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (Fin (w₀.length + 1)) where
+  q₀ := 0
+  tr := fun j _ _ =>
+    if h : (j : ℕ) < w₀.length then
+      tapeAction i 0 (some (some w₀[(j : ℕ)])) .pos ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩
+    else inputMoveAction 0 0
+
+/-- **R8.4′, the advancing writer, framed** (design §12.8a). From any
+configuration at state `0`, the writer returns to state `0` at exactly
+`|w₀| + 1`, and its states strictly between are not `0`. At that point the
+interval `[pos, pos + |w₀|)` of tape `i` holds `w₀`, whatever it held before,
+the head of tape `i` is at `pos + |w₀|`, and every other cell, every other
+head, the input position and the output are unchanged. Up to the return the
+head of tape `i` stays within `[pos, pos + |w₀|]`, and every other head is
+fixed. These are exactly the round hypotheses of `Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done`
+with round time `|w₀| + 1`.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the cells written: the state after `j ≤ |w₀|` steps
+is `j`, which is nonzero for `0 < j`, with `j` cells of `w₀` written and the
+head at `pos + j`. The last step is stationary and returns to `0`. No step
+reads a work cell. -/
+theorem writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
+    (w₀ : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (Fin (w₀.length + 1)) x)
+    (hstate : d.state = some 0) :
+    (writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d (w₀.length + 1) =
+        { d with
+          state := some 0
+          workTapes := fun j q =>
+            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ)
+              then FinTM.bufferTape w₀ (q - d.workTapePos j)
+            else d.workTapes j q
+          workTapePos := Function.update d.workTapePos i
+            (d.workTapePos i + (w₀.length : ℤ)) } ∧
+      (∀ t, 0 < t → t < w₀.length + 1 → ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some 0) ∧
+      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ w₀.length + 1 →
+        if j = i then
+          ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
+            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j) (d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ))
+        else ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ### R8.5a — the input copier -/
+
+/-- **R8.5a, the input copier** (design §12.8a). Copy the native input onto
+tape `i` from its head, the two heads moving right in lockstep, then walk both
+heads back together, guided by the input tape's left end marker. The phases are
+the sweep alphabet's: `sweep` copies, `rewind` returns, and `done` is the live
+exit anchor. The destination needs no left delimiter. -/
+def inputCopyTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Symbol SweepPhase where
+  q₀ := .sweep
+  tr := fun q inp _ =>
+    match q with
+    | .sweep =>
+      match inp with
+      | some s => tapeAction i 1 (some (some s)) .pos .sweep
+      | none => tapeAction i (-1) none .neg .rewind
+    | .rewind =>
+      match inp with
+      | some _ => tapeAction i (-1) none .neg .rewind
+      | none => tapeAction i 1 none .pos .done
+    | .done => inputMoveAction 0 .done
+
+/-- **R8.5a, the input copier, framed** (design §12.8a). From any configuration
+in the copy phase with the input head at position `1`, the copier reaches
+`done` at exactly `2|x| + 2` and not earlier, where `x` is the native input. At
+that point the interval `[pos, pos + |x|)` of tape `i` holds `x`, whatever it
+held before, and every other cell, every head, the input position and the
+output are unchanged. Up to the exit the head of tape `i` stays within
+`[pos - 1, pos + |x|]`, and every other head is fixed.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input cells: `|x|` lockstep steps copy `x`,
+and the input's right end marker turns both heads left. The return takes `|x|`
+lockstep steps over the input, and the left end marker supplies the entry step,
+which puts the input head back at `1` and the work head back at `pos`. -/
+theorem inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
+    (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some .sweep) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) :
+    (inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d (2 * x.length + 2) =
+        { d with
+          state := some .done
+          workTapes := fun j q =>
+            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (x.length : ℤ)
+              then FinTM.bufferTape x (q - d.workTapePos j)
+            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
+      (∀ t < 2 * x.length + 2, ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).state ≠ some .done) ∧
+      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 →
+        if j = i then
+          ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
+            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + (x.length : ℤ))
+        else ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ### R8.5d — the input fold -/
+
+/-- **R8.5d, the input fold** (design §12.8a). Read the native input left to
+right, updating a finite state by `δ` from `a₀`, then walk the input head back
+and enter the live anchor `done a` with the final state `a` as the verdict.
+No work tape is touched. With `δ` testing membership in the image of an
+embedding, it is the input validator of design §12.8a §0. -/
+def inputFoldTM {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} (k : ℕ) (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) :
+    MultiTapeTM k Γ (ScanPhase A) where
+  q₀ := .fwd a₀
+  tr := fun q inp _ =>
+    match q with
+    | .fwd a =>
+      match inp with
+      | some γ => inputMoveAction 1 (.fwd (δ a γ))
+      | none => inputMoveAction (-1) (.bwd a)
+    | .bwd a =>
+      match inp with
+      | some _ => inputMoveAction (-1) (.bwd a)
+      | none => inputMoveAction 1 (.done a)
+    | .done a => inputMoveAction 0 (.done a)
+
+/-- **R8.5d, the input fold, framed** (design §12.8a). From any configuration
+in the forward phase at `a₀` with the input head at position `1`, the fold
+reaches `done (x.foldl δ a₀)` at exactly `2|x| + 2`, where `x` is the native
+input, and no `done` anchor earlier. Nothing else changes: the finish is the
+start configuration with only the control state replaced, so the input head is
+back at `1`. Up to the exit no work head moves.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input cells: after `j ≤ |x|` forward steps the
+state is the fold of the first `j` symbols and the input head is at `j + 1`.
+The right end marker turns the head, `|x|` steps return it, and the left end
+marker supplies the entry step. -/
+theorem inputFoldTM_run_ofCfg {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ}
+    (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) (d : Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x)
+    (hstate : d.state = some (.fwd a₀)) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) :
+    (inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d (2 * x.length + 2) =
+        { d with state := some (.done (x.foldl δ a₀)) } ∧
+      (∀ t < 2 * x.length + 2, ∀ a,
+        ((inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some (.done a)) ∧
+      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 →
+        ((inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
+  sorry
+
+end Turing

@@ -172,10 +180,18 @@ private lemma seamComp_dispatch {Symbol : Type*} {x : List Symbol} [DecidableEq
   dsimp only [seamCompTM]
   rw [if_pos rfl, seam_stationary_apply]
 
-/-- The whole left trajectory agrees through the exit time.
+/-- **R8.8, the left prefix of a seam** (design §12.8a; promoted from the
+private `seamComp_left`, finding SC-4 of the §12.7 statement gate). If `M₁`,
+started from an arbitrary configuration `c`, avoids its exit anchor at every
+time strictly below `T`, then for every `t ≤ T` the composite started from the
+left-mapped `c` is at the left-mapped `M₁` configuration at `t`. No endpoint
+equation is required, and the endpoint itself is included. This is the
+trajectory statement a host with two exits needs on the branch it does not
+take.
+
 **Proof sketch.** Induct on the time; the cut licenses the left-step
 identity at every predecessor strictly before the endpoint. -/
-private lemma seamComp_left {Symbol : Type*} {x : List Symbol} [DecidableEq S₁]
+theorem seamCompTM_runFrom_left {Symbol : Type*} {x : List Symbol} [DecidableEq S₁]
     (M₁ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₁) (exit : S₁)
     (M₂ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₂) (entry : S₂)

+/-- **R8.8, the two-exit seam** (design §12.8a). Attach a continuation to each
+of two exit anchors of a host: `M₁` after `e₁` and `M₂` after `e₂`, by nesting
+two `Turing.seamCompTM`s. The host `M₀` with two live anchors is typically
+`Turing.counterLoopTM` with its `done` and `escape`. -/
+def seamCompTM₂ {Symbol : Type*} {S₀ : Type*} [DecidableEq S₀] [DecidableEq S₁]
+    (M₀ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₀) (e₁ e₂ : S₀) (M₁ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₁) (entry₁ : S₁)
+    (M₂ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₂) (entry₂ : S₂) :
+    MultiTapeTM k Symbol ((S₀ ⊕ S₁) ⊕ S₂) :=
+  seamCompTM (seamCompTM M₀ e₁ M₁ entry₁) (Sum.inl e₂) M₂ entry₂
+
+/-- **R8.8, the two-exit seam, general configurations** (design §12.8a).
+Suppose the host `M₀`, from an arbitrary configuration `c₀`, reaches `c₁` at
+exactly `T₀` and meets neither of the distinct anchors `e₁`, `e₂` earlier.
+If `c₁` is at `e₁`, then for every `t` the two-exit composite at `T₀ + 1 + t`
+is `M₁`'s run, from `c₁` with only the control state replaced by `entry₁`, at
+`t`, mapped into the composite's states; the `M₂` summand is never entered.
+Symmetrically, if `c₁` is at `e₂`, the composite at `T₀ + 1 + t` is `M₂`'s run
+from `c₁` at `entry₂`. The dispatch costs one stationary step in either branch,
+and the continuation runs unboundedly, halting included, so its own first-return
+and trajectory statements transfer.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Branch `e₁`: the outer seam's left machine is the inner
+composite, whose states stay away from the outer exit `Sum.inl e₂`: before
+`T₀` by the cut, at `T₀` because `e₁ ≠ e₂`, and afterwards because they are
+`Sum.inr` states or halted. So `Turing.seamCompTM_runFrom_left` for the outer
+seam reduces the run to the inner composite's, which `Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg`
+and the right lockstep of the inner seam evaluate. Branch `e₂`: the inner
+composite reaches `Sum.inl e₂` at `T₀` by `Turing.seamCompTM_runFrom_left`,
+never having met `e₁`, and the outer dispatch and right lockstep finish. -/
+theorem seamCompTM₂_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {S₀ : Type*} {x : List Symbol}
+    [DecidableEq S₀] [DecidableEq S₁]
+    (M₀ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₀) (e₁ e₂ : S₀) (he : e₁ ≠ e₂)
+    (M₁ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₁) (entry₁ : S₁) (M₂ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S₂) (entry₂ : S₂)
+    {c₀ c₁ : Cfg k Symbol S₀ x} {T₀ : ℕ}
+    (h₀ : M₀.runFrom c₀ T₀ = c₁)
+    (hcut : ∀ t < T₀, (M₀.runFrom c₀ t).state ≠ some e₁ ∧ (M₀.runFrom c₀ t).state ≠ some e₂) :
+    (c₁.state = some e₁ → ∀ t : ℕ,
+      (seamCompTM₂ M₀ e₁ e₂ M₁ entry₁ M₂ entry₂).runFrom
+          ((c₀.mapState Sum.inl).mapState Sum.inl) (T₀ + 1 + t) =
+        ((M₁.runFrom (c₁.mapState fun _ => entry₁) t).mapState Sum.inr).mapState Sum.inl) ∧
+    (c₁.state = some e₂ → ∀ t : ℕ,
+      (seamCompTM₂ M₀ e₁ e₂ M₁ entry₁ M₂ entry₂).runFrom
+          ((c₀.mapState Sum.inl).mapState Sum.inl) (T₀ + 1 + t) =
+        (M₂.runFrom (c₁.mapState fun _ => entry₂) t).mapState Sum.inr) := by
+  sorry
+
 variable {S : Type*}
 
 /-- **R3′, the fresh-entry/release adapter** (round-1 repair R3). The seam
diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..67f564a8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,226 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
+-/
+import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Finite
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 0
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+/-!
+# Running `Bool` machines on rich alphabets: the embedding transport
+
+A machine over a rich work alphabet `Γ` often needs a binary routine (a counter, a
+compare) on one of its tapes. Instead of re-proving each binary routine at `Γ`, this file
+**lifts** a `Bool` machine along an embedding `e : Bool ↪ Γ`. The lifted machine reads
+through `decodeBool e`, where foreign symbols read as blank, and writes and emits
+through `e`. From every lifted configuration and at every time it runs as the original,
+everything mapped along `e` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom`). It is the
+embedding analogue of the equivalence transport `Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols`
+(`Build/CounterLoop.lean`). Space is preserved exactly. A lifted computation is a
+computation *via* `e` in the sense `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` consumes, so a
+rich-alphabet construction can finish by alphabet reduction.
+
+Design: `machine-library-design.md` §12.8 (decision 12.8.1, rich-alphabet configuration
+records) and §12.8a R8.0. Consumers: the §12.8 record rows, which run the binary counter
+rows on dedicated digit tapes, and §13d's zone carrier, whose alphabet embeds `Bool` by
+`Sum.inl`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.decodeBool` — decoding along `e`; foreign symbols decode to `none`.
+* `Turing.Action.liftSymbols`, `Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols`, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`,
+  `Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols` — the lift of actions, configurations and machines.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom` — the transport: lifted runs are lifts of runs.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step` — its one-step form.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg`, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_spaceUsed` — start
+  configurations and space.
+* `Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia` — a lifted computation is a computation via
+  `e`, in the same time.
+
+## References
+
+* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Cambridge
+  University Press, 2009. (§1.2 and Claim 1.5: the alphabet of a machine can be changed at a
+  constant-factor cost; this file is the cost-free direction, from `Bool` into a larger
+  alphabet.)
+-/
+
+namespace Turing
+
+section Lift
+variable {k : ℕ} {Γ State : Type*}
+
+/-- Decode a rich symbol along `e : Bool ↪ Γ`: `e b` decodes to `some b`, and every
+symbol outside the image of `e` decodes to `none`, which the lifted machine reads as a
+blank. -/
+def decodeBool [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (γ : Γ) : Option Bool :=
+  if γ = e true then some true else if γ = e false then some false else none
+
+/-- Decoding inverts `e` on its image.
+
+**Proof sketch.** `cases b`; the two images differ by injectivity of `e`. -/
+@[simp] lemma decodeBool_apply [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (b : Bool) :
+    decodeBool e (e b) = some b := by
+  cases b
+  · have : e false ≠ e true := fun h => Bool.false_ne_true (e.injective h)
+    simp [decodeBool, this]
+  · simp [decodeBool]
+
+/-- Lift an action along `e`: written symbols and the emission are mapped by `e`. -/
+def Action.liftSymbols (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (a : Action k Bool State) : Action k Γ State where
+  inputTape := a.inputTape
+  workTapes := fun j => ((a.workTapes j).1.map (Option.map e), (a.workTapes j).2)
+  output := a.output.map e
+  state := a.state
+
+/-- Lift a configuration along `e`: input, work cells and output mapped by `e`. -/
+def Cfg.liftSymbols (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
+    Cfg k Γ State (x.map e) where
+  state := c.state
+  inputPos := Fin.cast (by simp) c.inputPos
+  workTapes := fun j p => (c.workTapes j p).map e
+  workTapePos := c.workTapePos
+  output := c.output.map e
+
+/-- Lift a machine along `e`: read through `decodeBool e`, write through `e`. -/
+def MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State) (e : Bool ↪ Γ) :
+    MultiTapeTM k Γ State where
+  q₀ := M.q₀
+  tr := fun q inp work =>
+    (M.tr q (inp.bind (decodeBool e)) fun j => (work j).bind (decodeBool e)).liftSymbols e
+
+/-- The lifted configuration reads the mapped input symbol.
+
+**Proof sketch.** The two input positions have the same value, so the end-marker cases
+match; an inner position reads `(x.map e)[i] = e x[i]`. -/
+lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
+    (c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol = c.inputSymbol.map e := by
+  have hv : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos : ℕ) = c.inputPos := rfl
+  unfold Cfg.inputSymbol
+  have e0 : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos = 0) ↔ (c.inputPos = 0) := by
+    simp only [Fin.ext_iff, hv, Fin.val_zero]
+  have e1 : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos = ((x.map e).length + 1 : ℕ)) ↔
+      (c.inputPos = (x.length + 1 : ℕ)) := by
+    simp only [hv, List.length_map]
+  by_cases h0 : c.inputPos = 0
+  · rw [dif_pos (e0.mpr h0), dif_pos h0]; rfl
+  · rw [dif_neg (fun h => h0 (e0.mp h)), dif_neg h0]
+    by_cases h1 : c.inputPos = (x.length + 1 : ℕ)
+    · rw [dif_pos (e1.mpr h1), dif_pos h1]; rfl
+    · rw [dif_neg (fun h => h1 (e1.mp h)), dif_neg h1]
+      simp [hv]
+
+/-- Moving the input head commutes with recasting the position type. -/
+private lemma moveInputPos_cast {n m : ℕ} (h : n + 2 = m + 2) (p : Fin (n + 2)) (s : SignType) :
+    moveInputPos (Fin.cast h p) s = Fin.cast h (moveInputPos p s) := by
+  have hnm : n = m := by omega
+  subst hnm
+  rfl
+
+/-- One step commutes with the lift.
+
+**Proof sketch.** A halted configuration does not move. Otherwise the lifted machine
+decodes the scanned symbols back to the original ones (`decodeBool_apply`), so it
+selects the lift of the original action; applying a lifted action to a lifted
+configuration is the lift of the applied action, cell by cell. -/
+lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
+    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
+    (M.liftSymbols e).step (c.liftSymbols e) = (M.step c).liftSymbols e := by
+  cases hs : c.state with
+  | none => simp [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.liftSymbols, hs]
+  | some q =>
+    have hin : (c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol.bind (decodeBool e) = c.inputSymbol := by
+      rw [Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol]; cases c.inputSymbol <;> simp
+    have hw : (fun j => ((c.liftSymbols e).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)) =
+        c.workTapeSymbols := by
+      funext j; simp only [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols]
+      cases c.workTapes j (c.workTapePos j) <;> simp
+    simp only [MultiTapeTM.step,
+      show (c.liftSymbols e).state = some q by simp [Cfg.liftSymbols, hs], hs]
+    change ((M.tr q ((c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol.bind (decodeBool e))
+      fun j => ((c.liftSymbols e).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)).liftSymbols e).apply
+        (c.liftSymbols e) = _
+    rw [hin, hw]
+    apply Cfg.ext
+    · rfl
+    · exact moveInputPos_cast (by simp) _ _
+    · funext j p
+      simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols]
+      cases (M.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols).workTapes j |>.1 with
+      | none => simp
+      | some v =>
+        simp only [Option.map_some]
+        by_cases hp : p = c.workTapePos j
+        · subst p; simp
+        · simp [Function.update_of_ne hp]
+    · rfl
+    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols, List.map_append]
+      cases (M.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols).output <;> rfl
+
+/-- **The embedding transport** (§12.8 R8.0): from every `Bool` configuration and at
+every time, the lifted machine runs as the original, with input, work cells and output
+mapped along `e`.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induction on `t` with `liftSymbols_step`. -/
+theorem MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
+    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) (t : ℕ) :
+    (M.liftSymbols e).runFrom (c.liftSymbols e) t = (M.runFrom c t).liftSymbols e := by
+  induction t generalizing c with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ t ih =>
+    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step,
+      MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step, ih]
+
+/-- The lift keeps the state. -/
+@[simp] lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_state (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
+    (c.liftSymbols e).state = c.state := rfl
+
+/-- The lift keeps the work-head positions. -/
+@[simp] lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_workTapePos (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool}
+    (c : Cfg k Bool State x) : (c.liftSymbols e).workTapePos = c.workTapePos := rfl
+
+/-- The lifted machine starts at the lift of the original start (both blank tapes, same
+heads and state). -/
+lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
+    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (x : List Bool) :
+    (M.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e) = (M.initCfg x).liftSymbols e := by
+  apply Cfg.ext <;> rfl
+
+/-- Space is preserved exactly: the head trajectories are the same.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Unfold the visited sets and rewrite with `liftSymbols_runFrom`. -/
+lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_spaceUsed [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
+    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) (t : ℕ) :
+    (M.liftSymbols e).spaceUsed (c.liftSymbols e) t = M.spaceUsed c t := by
+  simp [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape, MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead,
+    MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom]
+
+end Lift
+
+/-- The `FinTM` layer of the lift. -/
+def FinTM.liftSymbols {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (M : FinTM Bool) (e : Bool ↪ Γ) : FinTM Γ :=
+  ⟨M.k, M.State, M.tm.liftSymbols e⟩
+
+/-- A `Bool` machine computing `f` computes `f` via `e` when lifted, in the same time:
+the form `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` consumes.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Rewrite the lifted run from the lifted start with
+`liftSymbols_initCfg` and `liftSymbols_runFrom`; halting and the mapped output follow. -/
+theorem FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (M : FinTM Bool)
+    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {f : List Bool → List Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ} (h : M.ComputesFunInTime f T) :
+    (M.liftSymbols e).ComputesFunInTimeVia e f T := by
+  intro x
+  have hx := (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (h x)
+  refine (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_
+  change ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).runFrom ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e)) _).state = none ∧
+    ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).runFrom ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e)) _).output = _
+  rw [MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg, MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom]
+  exact ⟨hx.1, congrArg (List.map e) hx.2⟩
+
+end Turing

+#### 9. Statement gate, round 1: decisions and repairs (2026-10-11)
+
+Round 1 failed with 0 blockers, 1 major, 7 minors and 39 notes
+(`audits/s12-8-statements-findings.md`).
+
+**Decisions** (user, the auditor's recommendations, on the open questions
+of §8):
+
+1. Skip back stays the **inverse** of skip, at `|u| + 3`.
+2. Shared tables get a **fixed nonempty header field**, so seek end always
+   has a field to stop after. The table ends are two blank cells before the
+   header and two after the last field. From seek end's stopping blank, a
+   consumer reaches the table start by skipping back over the last field
+   and then seeking start. The deferred table rows are stated with this
+   layout.
+3. `writeAdvTM` stays **cyclic**. One-shot callers use `seamReleaseTM`.
+4. The record rows keep their **fixed local tape layouts**, and hosts embed
+   them by R1.
+5. The deferred record rows (validity, init, next, table append and find)
+   get **their own statement gate** with S1b's concrete layout, before
+   S1b's fill uses them. R8.0b and R8.5c are explicit prerequisites.
+6. The new modules are **wired into the `TuringMachine` facade** at this
+   gate: `SymbolLift`, `Build/CounterLoop`, `Build/Scan`, `Build/InputCall`
+   and `Build/CfgRecord`. Nine older files of the topic are also absent
+   from the facade; they are recorded as `backlog.md` FAC-1.
+7. G2's core is `scanTM`, and `copyMapTM`/`transferMapTM` stay for G3/G4
+   (§13d, G2).

+  bounded time but not the cells they visit, so they were too weak for
+  Savitch and logspace consumers. Each now bounds every work head, through
+  its verdict or exit, to `C·(size + 1)` cells of its entry position. The
+  size is the record's layout length for the step and test rows, `fs`'s
+  layout length for the equality row, and `|w|` for the seek. So the space
+  does not depend on how far the native input head travels, and repeated

## ===== audits/evidence/s12-8/S128R2SpaceProbe.lean.txt =====

import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputCall
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CfgRecord

set_option autoImplicit false

/-! §12.8 statement gate, round 2: adequacy probe (maintainer). A head-range clause of
the repaired form bounds `spaceUsed`, so the repaired record step and input seek
give their consumers a work-space bound that does not depend on the native input
head. -/

namespace Turing

/-- A run whose work heads stay within `R` cells of their entry positions visits at
most `2R + 1` cells per tape. -/
theorem probe_spaceUsed_le_of_heads {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*} {x : List Symbol}
    (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (d : Cfg k Symbol State x) (t R : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin k,
      |(M.runFrom d u).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤ (R : ℤ)) :
    M.spaceUsed d t ≤ k * (2 * R + 1) := by
  calc M.spaceUsed d t = ∑ i, M.spaceUsedByTape d t i := rfl
    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin k, (2 * R + 1) := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => by
      unfold MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead
      have hsub : (Finset.range (t + 1)).image (fun t' => (M.runFrom d t').workTapePos i) ⊆
          Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos i - R) (d.workTapePos i + R) := by
        intro z hz
        obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
        have hb := h u (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hu)) i
        rw [abs_le] at hb
        exact Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨by linarith [hb.1], by linarith [hb.2]⟩
      calc _ ≤ (Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos i - R) (d.workTapePos i + R)).card :=
            Finset.card_le_card hsub
        _ = 2 * R + 1 := by rw [Int.card_Icc]; omega
    _ = k * (2 * R + 1) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_const_nat fun _ _ => rfl, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

/-- The repaired input seek: up to its exit, work space `O(|w| + 1)` at every input
position and input length. -/
example : ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Fintype S) (_ : DecidableEq S) (R : MultiTapeTM 2 Bool S)
    (entry exit : S) (C : ℕ),
    ∀ {x : List Bool} (p : ℕ) (w : List Bool), Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) = p →
      p ≤ x.length + 1 → ∀ d : Cfg 2 Bool S x, d.state = some entry →
      (∀ q : ℤ, -1 ≤ q → q ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
        d.workTapes 0 (d.workTapePos 0 + q) = FinTM.bufferTape w q) →
      (∀ q, d.workTapes 1 q = none) →
      ∃ t, (R.runFrom d t).state = some exit ∧
        R.spaceUsed d t ≤ 2 * (2 * (C * (w.length + 1)) + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨S, i1, i2, R, entry, exit, C, h⟩ := exists_inputSeekTM
  refine ⟨S, i1, i2, R, entry, exit, C, fun p w hp hpx d hd hw h1 => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨t, -, -, hheads, hexit, -⟩ := h p w hp hpx d hd hw h1
  exact ⟨t, hexit, probe_spaceUsed_le_of_heads R d t _ hheads⟩

/-- The repaired record step: up to its verdict, work space linear in the record
length, however long the native input is. -/
example {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} [Fintype Q] [DecidableEq Q] [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
    (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool Q) (upd : T → Option Bool → T) (hupd : ∀ τ, upd τ none = τ) :
    ∃ (K : ℕ) (P : Type) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : DecidableEq P)
      (R : MultiTapeTM (K + 1) (RecSym Q T) P) (entry yes no : P) (C : ℕ), yes ≠ no ∧
      ∀ {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), c.InWindow s →
      ∀ d : Cfg (K + 1) (RecSym Q T) P (x.map (RecSym.digitEmb Q T)),
        d.state = some entry → RecordAt d 0 (cfgRecord s c τ) →
        (∀ j : Fin (K + 1), j ≠ 0 → ∀ p, d.workTapes j p = none) →
        ∃ t, R.spaceUsed d t ≤
          (K + 1) * (2 * (C * ((joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length + 1)) + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨K, P, i1, i2, R, entry, yes, no, C, hyn, h⟩ := exists_recordStepTM M upd hupd
  refine ⟨K, P, i1, i2, R, entry, yes, no, C, hyn, fun s c τ hc d hd hrec hblank => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨t, -, -, hheads, -⟩ := h s c τ hc d hd hrec hblank
  exact ⟨t, probe_spaceUsed_le_of_heads R d t _ hheads⟩

end Turing
